quarterly_data.quarter: Lynas Rare Earths results release: FY26 Results Announcement (08-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: FY26 results (year to June 30, 2026; AUD): revenue $977.9m (FY25 $556.5m), net profit after tax $222.4m (FY25 $8.0m), EBITDA $386.0m, EBIT $247.4m, cost of sales $585.5m; closing cash, cash equivalents and short-term deposits $1,209.1m (FY25 $166.5m). NdPr sales volume rose 12% to 7,337 tonnes (record NdPr production in the second half) and total REO sales 11% to 12,122 tonnes, at a record average selling price of A$80.7/kg REO, reflecting higher market prices, more heavy rare earth sales and sales with pricing not linked to the market index. Higher cost of sales reflected higher fixed costs of new facilities in commissioning and ramp-up, higher costs of sourcing inputs outside China and geopolitical cost escalation. Interim CEO Pol Le Roux: demand for rare earth permanent magnets in outside-China markets remains strong.
quarterly_data.figure: FY26 revenue $977.9m (FY25 $556.5m); NPAT $222.4m; NdPr sales 7,337 t (+12%); average price A$80.7/kg REO

quarterly_data.quarter: Lynas Rare Earths results release: FY26 Results Announcement (08-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Offtake agreements (FY26 results release): the updated 12-year availability and supply agreement with Japan Australia Rare Earths B.V. (JARE), announced in March 2026, includes firm offtake of 5,000 tonnes per annum of NdPr with a US$110/kg NdPr floor price and upside sharing above US$150/kg capped at US$10m per annum; Lynas will also make up to 7,200 tonnes per annum of NdPr available to Japanese industry to 2038, and the agreement includes firm offtake of 50% of all heavy rare earth oxides, with up to 75% made available to the Japanese market (subject to no opportunity loss to Lynas). Lynas also has a floor price agreement with the U.S. Government for supply to the U.S. industrial base over a four-year period.
quarterly_data.figure: JARE firm offtake 5,000 tpa NdPr at a US$110/kg floor; up to 7,200 tpa to 2038; 50% of HRE oxides

quarterly_data.quarter: Lynas Rare Earths results release: FY26 Results Announcement (08-26-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Operations and growth (FY26 results release): first production of samarium (Sm) oxide in Malaysia in March 2026, adding to dysprosium and terbium oxides first produced in FY25; Lynas Malaysia's operating licence was renewed for 10 years from March 3, 2026; an expanded heavy rare earths separation facility at Lynas Malaysia was announced; at Kalgoorlie, process modifications including continuous precipitation were completed and a water recycle plant is being completed, after electricity supply problems in the December quarter stabilised in the second half; the Mt Weld hybrid renewable power station has been fully operational since January 2026 (93% renewable electricity in H2 FY26) and the Mt Weld Carbonatite scoping study is complete. Under 'Towards 2030' it signed a long-term partnership agreement with JS Link, Inc. in July 2026 for JS Link to develop a rare earth permanent magnet factory in Kuantan, Malaysia, an MoU with Noveon Magnetics (October 2025) for a U.S. magnet supply chain, and a framework agreement with LS Eco Energy (March 2026) toward long-term metal processing at a new rare earth metal plant LS Eco Energy will build in Vietnam.
quarterly_data.figure: Sm oxide first produced March 2026; Malaysian licence renewed for 10 years; 93% renewable electricity at Mt Weld in H2 FY26
